subject: sentences
title: Person, Place or Thing
about: A naming word (noun) names a person, a place or a thing: he sorts teacher, park and spoon, finds the naming word in a short sentence, and spots the special names that get a capital letter (Mia, not girl). Common and proper nouns are the Nouns row of NC's K-1 grammar continuum under L.1.1, and this level builds on Naming, action, describing.
tip: Ask the sorting question out loud: is it someone, is it somewhere you can go, or is it something you can hold?

cards.q: A teacher: is it a person, a place or a thing?
cards.note: A teacher is a person. A naming word names a person, a place or a thing.

cards.q: Park is a naming word. Is it a person, a place or a thing?
cards.note: A park is a place. You can go to a park.

cards.q: A spoon: is it a person, a place or a thing?
cards.note: A spoon is a thing. You can hold it in your hand.

cards.q: Doctor is a naming word. Is it a person, a place or a thing?
cards.note: A doctor is a person who helps you get well.

cards.q: A beach: is it a person, a place or a thing?
cards.note: A beach is a place. You can go to the beach.

cards.q: Drum is a naming word. Is it a person, a place or a thing?
cards.note: A drum is a thing. You can tap it and carry it.

cards.q: The red cup fell. Which word is a naming word?
cards.note: Cup names a thing. Red tells what it is like, and fell is an action.

cards.q: Mia runs fast. Which word names a person?
cards.note: Mia is a person, so her name is a naming word. Runs is an action.

cards.q: We sat on the soft rug. Which word names a thing?
cards.note: Rug names a thing. Sat is an action and soft tells what the rug is like.

cards.q: Sam went to the big park. Which word names a place?
cards.note: Park names a place. Sam is a naming word too, but Sam is a person.

cards.q: The wet dog ran in. Which word is a naming word?
cards.note: Dog names an animal, and an animal is a thing you can touch. Wet describes it and ran is an action.

cards.q: Which one is a special name that gets a capital letter?
cards.note: Mia is one special girl, so her name gets a capital. Girl and kid can mean any girl or any kid.

cards.q: Which one is a special name?
cards.note: Max is a special name for one boy, so it starts with a capital M.

cards.q: Which word can name any boy at all?
cards.note: Boy can mean any boy, so it has no capital. Ben and Jon are special names for one boy each.

cards.q: Zoe is a girl. Which word is her special name?
cards.note: Zoe is her special name, so it gets a capital. Girl could be any girl.

cards.q: Ben has a cat named Dot. Which word is the cat's special name?
cards.note: Dot is the special name of one cat, so it gets a capital. Cat could be any cat.

cards.q: Which one starts with a capital because it is a name?
cards.note: Liv is a special name, so it gets a capital. Pup and hen can name any pup or any hen.
